source.title: Implicit bias of deep linear networks in the large learning rate phase
source.authors: Wei Huang; Wei-Tao Du; R. Xu; Chunrui Liu

record.tranche_reason: Tests how learning-rate phases relate to held-out accuracy for linear networks on a CIFAR-10 binary classification task, extending the generalization study to a large-learning-rate setting.
record.gate_note: Reports CIFAR-10 held-out accuracy by learning-rate phase and stopping strategy. The theoretical loss, NTK and Hessian results do not measure a version's named gap or sharpness property; cited results from other work are not extracted.
record.test_reason: The study tests learning-rate phases and annealing in deep linear networks, which none of V1–V8 names. Its Hessian and NTK results do not test V7's magnitude-aware perturbation measure or its relationship to the training–test error gap.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors argue that catapult-phase training reaches flatter minima for non-separable data and can improve generalization in linear networks. Their CIFAR-10 results qualify this: large learning rates benefit fixed-step comparisons and annealed training, but perform worse without annealing under the alternative stopping rule.
record.recipe_differences: Studies deep linear networks trained with full-batch gradient descent and logistic or exponential loss, emphasizing large learning-rate phases; the CIFAR-10 experiment uses a binary subset and learning-rate annealing.
record.method_sensitivity: Test accuracy varies with learning-rate phase and stopping strategy: fixed training step, fixed physical time, and subsequent learning-rate annealing.

fits_no_version.finding: For both linear architectures on the CIFAR-10 binary task, catapult-phase learning rates give better test accuracy at fixed step counts, worse accuracy under the alternative stopping rule without decay, and the best accuracy after annealing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The generalization benefit of large learning rates in deep linear networks depends on stopping strategy and subsequent learning-rate annealing.

record.problems: The real-data experiment is limited to two CIFAR-10 categories and two linear-network architectures. Accuracy values are presented in figures without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The paper notes that fixed training time favors larger learning rates because they run faster.
record.rows_left_out: Theoretical and synthetic-data results on training loss, NTK eigenvalues and Hessian curvature were left out because they do not measure the behavior named in the claim versions. Figure 3 reports curvature and NTK against learning rate, but does not test the magnitude-aware sharpness and training-test-gap relationship in V7.

untested.parts: No comparison of random-label memorization and natural-label generalization using the same architecture and training recipe.
No width sweep beyond the width needed to fit the training data.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks or local connectivity.
No comparison of adaptive optimizers with SGD or momentum SGD.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets.
No magnitude-scaled weight perturbations, training–test gap ranking, or comparison with norm- and margin-based measures in a convolutional family.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The record's T3 classification should be T6 relative to these specific versions. Figure 3 measures unscaled Hessian curvature on synthetic data, not V7's named sharpness measure. The paper's main-text physical-time notation and Figure 4 caption are inconsistent; the caption supplies the operational stopping schedule. Exact accuracy values cannot be recovered reliably from the supplied figure text.

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare fitting natural labels with fitting random labels.
Does not sweep network width past the zero-training-error threshold.
Uses linear networks; does not compare convolutional and fully connected image models.
Does not compare adaptive optimizers with SGD.
Does not vary batch size or compare large- and small-batch training.
Measures Hessian curvature and NTK eigenvalues, but does not test magnitude-scaled weight perturbations or compare sharpness measures as predictors of the training-test gap.

rows.subject: two-layer linear network without bias
rows.operation_detail: Trained with logistic loss at different learning rates; test accuracy measured at fixed training step.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, cars and dogs binary classification

rows.note: Authors state that learning rates in the catapult phase have the advantage in this fixed-training-time setting and that optimal performance is obtained in the catapult phase.
rows.check: Higher test accuracy in the catapult phase at 500 training steps measures a learning-rate effect outside all versions; observed is not a state for any supplied version.
